subject: Poisson likelihood with identity link function

messages.author: 2dc7aaeba1e88336
messages.subject: Poisson likelihood with identity link function
parts:
Hello, R-INLA members.

I tried to apply Poisson likelihood on besagproper latent variables with identity link function as following:

data <- data.frame(y = obs.data, idx = idx)
r <- inla(y ~ -1 + f(idx, model = "besagproper", graph = graph.filename),
             data = data, family = "poisson",
             control.family = list(control.link = list(model = "identity")), E = 1)

but

Link function `identity' is not valid or yet implemented.

returned.

How can I run this model?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Poisson likelihood with identity link function
parts:
This would be the model, like

y ~ Poisson(eta)

where eta is the linear predictor, but eta>0. does not match well with
being Gaussian. it only make sense if eta is >> 0.
you can add the identity link, but it is on your own risk. I would add
an offset to make it start from something positive.

you can add the identity link, using this 'hack'

> library(INLA)
> r=inla.models()
> ls(envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
[1] "hgid" "inla.models" "inla.options"
> m = get("inla.models", envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m$likelihood$poisson$link
[1] "default" "log" "logoffset"
"quantile" "test1" "special1"
[7] "special2"
> m$likelihood$poisson$link = c(m$likelihood$poisson$link, "identity")
> assign("inla.models", m, envir = INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m = get("inla.m> library(INLA)
> r=inla.models()
> ls(envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())

> m$likelihood$poisson$link = c(m$likelihood$poisson$link, "identity")
> assign("inla.models", m, envir = INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m = get("inla.models", envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m$likelihood$poisson$link
[1] "default" "log" "logoffset"
"quantile" "test1" "special1"

>

and you can move on from there. recall to add

y ~ offset(off) + ....

and define off = rep(10, n), or something. just subtract 10 later.

cannot guarentee anything here...

Thanks, Prof. Rue!

I could resolve the error with the suggested hack.
In my configuration, the offset technique is very effective because non-negativity of linear predictor eta is guaranteed.

But unfortunately another computational problem was occurred in optimization.
When I use log link function, the error did not raised.
And eta is in range about 1 - 50, therefore it is cannot assumed that scaling issue.

I would like to know your view.

[[[ some confusion the previous code in the my last email ]]]

This would be the model, like

        y ~ Poisson(eta)

where eta is the linear predictor, but eta>0. does not match well with
being Gaussian. it only make sense if eta is >> 0.
you can add the identity link, but it is on your own risk. I would add
an offset to make it start from something positive.

you can add the identity link, using this 'hack'

> library(INLA)
> r=inla.models()
> ls(envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
[1] "hgid"         "inla.models"  "inla.options"
> m = get("inla.models", envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m$likelihood$poisson$link
[1] "default"   "log"       "logoffset"
"quantile"  "test1"     "special1"
[7] "special2"
> m$likelihood$poisson$link = c(m$likelihood$poisson$link, "identity")
> assign("inla.models", m, envir = INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m = get("inla.models", envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
> m$likelihood$poisson$link
[1] "default"   "log"       "logoffset"
"quantile"  "test1"     "special1"
[7] "special2"  "identity"


and you can move on from there.  recall to add

        y ~ offset(off) + ....

and define off = rep(10, n), or something. just subtract 10 later.

cannot guarentee anything here...

H

you have to do like this, where you have to input an positive initial
value for the predictor, the first 'n' elements of 'x', and the rest of
that one, just fill with zero's.

if you have 'theta's you need to add those as well.

it will not like y=0's....

library(INLA)
r=inla.models()
ls(envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
m = get("inla.models", envir=INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())
m$likelihood$poisson$link = c(m$likelihood$poisson$link, "identity")
assign("inla.models", m, envir = INLA:::inla.get.inlaEnv())

n = 100
x = rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)
lambda = 50 + x
y = rpois(n, lambda = lambda)

y[y==0] = 1
r = inla(y ~ 1 + x,
family = "poisson",
control.mode = list(theta = numeric(), x = c(rep(100, n), 0,
0), restart=TRUE),
data = data.frame(y, x),

control.family = list(control.link = list(model =
"identity")))
summary(r)
